thread:
sarah: Heads-up — ACME (acct-acme-77) on Dedicated keeps getting 429s despite reserved pool rp-42 assigned. Customer says errors spike during short bursts, avg usage under committed. They also reported occasional 401s in the same timeframe. Can someone triage?

mike: Got a sample response from them? 429 body/headers matter (retry-after, remaining).

sarah: Pasted their response headers below (sanitized):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Limit: 200
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Reset: 24
Retry-After: 5
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error":"rate_limit_exceeded", "scope":"tenant" }
```

julia: Quick note: reserved pools have two controls — committed_qps and burst_window capacity. If their burst > bucket_size it will hit 429 even if average stays under committed. Also check mapping: API key must be bound to rp-42, otherwise requests route to shared capacity with stricter caps.

kevin: Agree. Runtime enforces per-tenant token-bucket + per-pool smoothing. Seen this when customer sends 8s bursts @ 400 RPS while committed_qps=200 with bucket_size=100. Token-bucket drains quickly. Logs show throttles: 
```
[2026-03-14T12:34:01Z] throttle tenant=acct-acme-77 pool=rp-42 limit=200 bucket=0 burst_window_ms=10000 action=throttle code=429
```

kevin: Also those intermittent 401s — might be rotated keys hitting wrong binding which causes routing to fallback and then auth failure if key invalid.

olivia: Checked billing/accounting — customer purchased "Reserved - Standard 200rps" on 2026-03-01 and we provisioned rp-42. However onboarding job #onboard-927 failed to attach a route tag for one API key (key-id key-zz7). That key will route to shared and be subject to different quotas.

sarah: Good catch. So two simultaneous issues: improper key->pool mapping causing auth/fallback, and burst pattern exceeding bucket. Action items?

mike: Short term: instruct customer to use a single key bound to rp-42 and smooth bursts (client side rate limiter). Provide them a curl repro they can run to see 429s locally.

ops-bot: Runbook link: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/reserved-pool-throttle> (steps 1-6).

sarah: Repro snippet I suggested to customer (curl + jq):
```bash
for i in {1..100}; do \
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer KEY_GOES_HERE" \ 
    -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"x"}' &
  if (( i % 20 == 0 )); then wait; fi
done
```

kevin: To verify token bucket behavior on our side, ops can run: 
```bash
rtcli inspect-bucket --pool rp-42 --tenant acct-acme-77
# returns: committed_qps=200, bucket_size=120, refill_ms=1000, last_refill=...
```

julia: If bucket_size too small relative to burst, recommend increasing bucket_size OR enabling rate_smoothing in pool config. Example config patch: 
```json
{"pool_id":"rp-42","rate_smoothing":true,"bucket_size":600}
```

olivia: I'll re-run the onboarding job to attach the missing tag to key-zz7 and confirm. If customer wants immediate relief, we can rebind their active key to rp-42 from console (requires approval).

mike: Ops, please tail the runtime logs around the timestamps Sarah pasted, check for consecutive throttle events and any 401s that line up. If we see many 429s from the pool alone, that's expected from the bucket behavior. If we see mix of 401 then 429, it's the mapping problem.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: redeploy of onboarding-worker succeeded at 1998765450 (onboard-927 re-run queued).

olivia: Confirmed rebind done at 1998765489 — key-zz7 now tagged -> rp-42. Sent customer note to rotate keys and test again.

sarah: Customer ran repro after rebind and says 401s disappeared but still gets 429s during same burst pattern. Suggested mitigation: client-side smoothing OR we can increase their bucket_size for a short promo window. Customer requested quick increase while they implement smoothing.

kevin: I can temporarily bump bucket_size to 500 for rp-42 tenant acct-acme-77; will monitor latency/cost. Ops please approve change in infra.

mike: Approve. Also set monitoring alert: if 429 rate > 5% sustained for 5m post-change, rollback.

sarah: Thanks team. I'll update ticket with repro, runbook link, and next steps (temp bucket bump + customer smoothing).

olivia: Billing note: we'll reconcile onboarding failure credit separately; nothing blocks capacity change.

sarah: Closing loop — will post follow-up if 429s persist after bump. :thumbsup:
